To cut a release, push a git tag on `main` in the form `vYYYY.MM.N`, for example `v2026.09.2`. The `N` is the sequence number within that month. For October 2026 the first tag would be `v2026.10.1`.

```
git checkout main && git pull
git tag v2026.10.1
git push origin v2026.10.1
```

CI does the rest. It builds the artifacts, runs the full test suite and publishes the release. Don't publish packages by hand.

This comes from the project's stored release-process memory. I didn't find a release script or CI config in the repo to check it against, so I haven't confirmed the CI side. I also haven't checked which tags already exist, so look at `git tag` before choosing `N`.
